findings.summary: EC-1's bare-name-import requirement was scoped only to the 4 explicitly-mocked symbols; it must generalize to every name run_budgeted calls that moves into a new submodule (e.g. _close_process_pipes, _read_capped), or a qualified-access regression on an unmocked-today name would silently stop being patchable in future tests without failing loudly now
findings.primary_agent_verification: independently confirmed via grep on scripts/antares/sandbox_budget.py (run_budgeted body, lines 369-540) and sandbox_budget_test.py: run_budgeted calls _read_capped and _close_process_pipes in addition to the 4 EC-1-named functions; also found an additional undocumented dependency, _drop_privileges (line 54, re-exported from sandbox_runner.py/T2c-1), accessed directly by the test at line 64 as _MODULE._drop_privileges() -- this one requires no change since it stays in the core file under the proposed split, but EC-1 didn't say so explicitly
findings.disposition: accepted, EC-1 rewritten to state the general rule plus the _drop_privileges no-op case explicitly

findings.summary: ambiguity between "zero modifications" to test assertions and "import wiring may be touched" -- risked the implementer changing which file/entrypoint the test loads via importlib
findings.primary_agent_verification: valid drafting gap, no repo evidence needed to confirm the ambiguity itself
findings.disposition: accepted, acceptance criteria now require both test files keep loading their target via spec_from_file_location pointed at the existing core file name, not a new __init__.py/package entrypoint
